reviewed_scope: For every real epsilon > 0, the tangent extension is globally differentiable and convex on the real line.
The pair has two jointly convex scalar coordinates on all of R^2 and is monotone in the product order on all of R^2.
Both output streams are nonnegative on the nonnegative input orthant.
The pair difference recovers the inverse square root of epsilon plus represented variance whenever the represented variance is nonnegative; independent streams may be signed.
definition_checks: Left branch equals the tangent at represented variance zero, with matching value epsilon^(-1/2) and derivative -(1/2)*epsilon^(-3/2).
The derivative is constant on the negative branch and increases toward zero on the nonnegative branch.
The positive profile adds M*z and has derivative between zero and M; the generic asymmetric lift yields exactly r(x-y)+M*x.
The negative head is exactly M*x; its subtraction cancels the common tilt.
Real powers are only used with positive bases in the inverse-square-root recovery and derivative arguments.
boundary_checks: At epsilon=1 and streams=(0,0), the pair is (1,0).
At epsilon=1 and streams=(0,1), the pair is (3/2,0), explicitly exercising the affine extension outside the recovery domain.
On the entire diagonal (a,a), including negative a, the difference is inverse sqrt(epsilon).
Global isotonicity accepts independent signed streams.
Recovery accepts any signed streams whose difference is nonnegative.
limits: This module proves a normalization primitive, not a complete LayerNorm or Transformer graph-composition theorem.
Epsilon must be strictly positive; the zero-epsilon boundary is not included.
No floating-point stability or practical efficiency result is established. The tilt grows as epsilon^(-3/2).
superseded_run: The initial six-contract ExactTypes.lean run was terminated after the final two contracts were added; only the eight-contract ExactTypesAll.lean run is acceptance evidence.
